Counsel for the appellants.

: Mr. P.C. Bisht, learned Additional Chief
Standing Counsel for the State of
Uttarakhand.
Counsel for the respondents. : Mr. M.C. Pant, learned counsel.
Mr. Birendra Singh Adhikari, learned
counsel.
Ms. Neetu Singh, learned counsel.
Mr. Kundan Singh Negi, learned counsel.
COMMON JUDGMENT : (per Hon 'ble Th e Ch ief Ju st ice Ms. Rit u Bah r i)
 For the reasons stated in the applications
seeking condonation of delay, Delay Condonation
Applications in all these Special Appeals are allowed, and
the delay in filing these Special Appeals is condoned.
2. This order shall dispose of above m entioned 37
cases, as comm on questions of facts and law are involved
in them. For the sake of convenience, facts of Special
Appeal No. 08/ 2018 are being taken into consideration.
3. The State has com e up in Appeal against the
judgment of the learned Single Judge dated 29.03.2017
passed in WPSS No. 1824/ 2016 and connected cases,
whereby the Writ Petitions filed by the respondent-writ
petitioners have been allowed, and the impugned orders

2024:UHC:6210-DB
11
dated 17.08.2016, 23.08.2016 and 31.08.2016 have
been quashed, and set-aside.
4. Respondents-writ petitioners were appointed as
Tube Well Operators in the erstwhile State of Uttar
Pradesh in the year 1992. Vide judgm ent dated
18.05.1994, the Allahabad High Court allowed the Writ
Petitions filed by the respondents-writ petitioners. The
Special Leave Petition filed by the State of Uttar Pradesh
against the above-said judgment of the Allahabad High
Court was dismissed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court on
03.03.1998.
5. Pursuant to the above-said judgm ent of the
Allahabad High Court, the respondents-writ petitioners
were granted the benefit of 1st ACP on 18.05.1992, and
2
nd ACP on 18.05.1998.
6. However, the respondents-writ petitioners were
allocated to the State of Uttarakhand, after promulgation
of the U.P. Reorganization Act, 2000. The State of
Uttarakhand, vide order dated 23.08.2016 issued an
order for recovering the benefits of the 1st and 2nd ACP
granted to the respondents-writ petitioners on
18.05.1992 and 18.05.1998. This notice was issued on

2024:UHC:6210-DB
12
the ground that the respondents-writ petitioners were not
working against any sanctioned post, and hence they
were not entitled for ACP.
7. The learned Single Judge has examined this
issue, and has held that the respondents-writ petitioners
were granted the benefit of parity at par with the
regularly appointed Tube Well Operators by the judgment
of the Allahabad High Court dated 18.05.1994, which was
upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court vide order dated
03.03.1998, and this parity could not be disturbed by
issuing Office Order dated 02.12.2000, as valuable rights
had accrued to the respondents-writ petitioners, as per
the judgment of the Allahabad High Court dated
18.05.1994.
8. The respondents-writ petitioners have been
regularized in service in the years 2013 & 2014, after
serving since 1992. Since the benefit of ACP was granted
to them way-back in the year 1992, the recovery was
being m ade by issuing a notice in the year 2016, i.e. after
a gap of 24 years. The learned Single Judge has rightly
referred to the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in
the case of St at e of Pu n j ab an d ot h er s v . Raf iq Masih

2024:UHC:6210-DB
13
( W h it e W ash er ) an d ot h er s, ( 2 0 1 5 ) 4 SCC 3 3 4 ,
wherein the Suprem e Court had m entioned the
circumstances, under which recovery cannot be effected.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the above-said case, has
observed as under :
"1 8 . I t is not possible to postulate all situations of
hardship which would govern employees on the issue of
recovery, where payments have mistakenly been made
by the employer, in excess of their entitlement. Be that
as it may, based on the decisions referred to
hereinabove, we may, as a ready reference, summarise
the following few situations, wherein recoveries by the
employers, would be impermissible in law :
(i) Recovery from the employees belonging to
Class I I I and Class I V service (or Group C and
Group D service).
(ii) Recovery from the retired employees, or
employees who are due to retire within one year,
of the order of recovery.
(iii) Recovery from employees, when the excess
payment has been made for a period in excess of
five years, before the order of recovery is issued.
(iv) Recovery in cases where an employee has
wrongfully been required to discharge duties of a
higher post, and has been paid accordingly, even
though he should have rightfully been required to
work against an inferior post.
(v) I n any other case, where the court arrives
at the conclusion, that recovery if made from the
employee, would be iniquitous or harsh or
arbitrary to such an extent, as would far
outweigh the equitable balance of the employer's
right to recover."
9. I n the present case, since the recovery was
sought to be done after a gap of 24 years vide impugned
orders dated 17.08.2016, 23.08.2016 and 31.08.2016,

2024:UHC:6210-DB
14
the Writ Petitions had rightly been allowed by the learned
Single Judge, while observing that no recovery can be
effected after a gap of 24 years from the above-said
em ployees, who belong to Group I V service, as it is not a
case that they have taken this benefit on account of
m aking any misrepresentation. This benefit was granted
to them as per the judgm ent of Allahabad High Court
dated 18.05.1994, which was upheld by the Hon'ble
Suprem e Court vide order dated 03.03.1998. The
present Special Appeals, in this backdrop, are liable to be
dismissed.
10. A similar issue of recovery came up before this
Court in Special Appeal No. 223/ 2022 and connected
cases. I n the said cases, the issue involved was that,
after granting the benefit of ad hoc service to Shiksha
Bandhus, they were granted the benefit of Selection
Grade of Rs. 7500-12000 with Grade Pay of Rs. 5400/ -,
as per Governm ent Order No. 655/ Madhyamik/ 2002
dated 12.07.2002. The benefit was granted to them on
27.08.2016, and the State Governm ent, thereafter,
withdrew the said benefit, vide Office Order dated
08.12.2017 and 13.12.2017. The Writ Petitions filed
challenging the above-said orders were allowed by the

2024:UHC:6210-DB
15
learned Single Judge on the ground that, once they have
been granted ad hoc status on 31.01.2006, then after
serving for 10 years, they have a right to be given the
benefit of Selection Grade, as per the Governm ent Order
of 2002. The fact that they were regularized in
Decem ber, 2013 could not be m ade a ground to withdraw
the benefit of Selection Grade.
11. While dismissing the above-said Special
Appeals filed by the State, it was observed that, as per
the Governm ent Order dated 12.07.2002, for grant of
Selection Grade, there was no condition that they should
have been appointed on a regularly sanctioned post, and
there was no condition that they should be regularized.
The said Special Appeals were dism issed by this Court.
12. Even in the present case, the benefit of 1st and
2
nd ACP was granted to the respondents-writ petitioners,
as per the judgm ent of the Allahabad High Court dated
18.05.1994, which was upheld by the Hon'ble Suprem e
Court vide order dated on 03.03.1998, and recovery was
being sought to be m ade in the year 2016, after a gap of
24 years.

2024:UHC:6210-DB
16
13. Counsel for the State has referred to the
Government Order dated 2nd Decem ber, 2000 to contend
that the benefit of ACP/ selection grade can only be given
to the incum bent, who have been regularized in service,
and the services rendered after regularization can be
m ade basis for grant of ACP. The G.O. dated 2nd
Decem ber, 2000, was issued by the Principal Secretary
Finance, Uttar Pradesh Governm ent (Annexure-10 to the
writ petition). By this G.O., approval has been granted to
the recomm endation of the Pay Com mittee (1997-99). A
perusal of the G.O. dated 2nd Decem ber, 2000 shows that
the first increment is to be granted to the employees/
officers, who have com pleted eight years of continuous
and satisfactory service on a post on or before 1st
January, 1996, and the benefit of selection grade is to be
allowed under the time scale and pay scale. The above
said G.O. does not m ention, whether the eight years
continuous satisfactory service should be post
regularization. The policy further m akes it clear that the
officers/ em ployees, who have rendered six years
continuous service before the date of availing the
selection grade pay or 14 years continuous service are
eligible for the pay-scale requirem ents.

2024:UHC:6210-DB
17
14. The next condition is Condition No. 2 of this
G.O. dated 2nd Decem ber, 2000, which clarifies that all
officers/ em ployees who have availed the benefit of
selection grade, and have served for six years or 14 years
continuous satisfactory service, they will be entitled for
prom otion if their services have been regularized on the
concerned post.
15. I t further provides that the next pay scale in
the post should be allowed individually, and it further
provides that if the em ployees have availed the benefit
after serving ten years then for the purpose, the period of
benefit of selection grade is restricted to only four years.
After availing the benefit of selection grade for the
prom otion/ admissibility of the next pay scale, it is
necessary for an em ployee to be regular in the relevant
post. Hence, for availing the benefit of selection grade
twice, there is no m andatory condition that he should be
regularized, and after availing the benefit of two selection
grades, for further prom otion, the em ployee has to be
regular. Rest of Condition Nos. 3 and 4 regulate the
prom otion after being regularised. Hence, for the
purposes of grant of two selection grades one after

2024:UHC:6210-DB
18
rendering six years of service and other after rendering
14 years of service, nowhere provides for service
rendered after regularization.
16. I n the facts of the present case, the
respondent-writ petitioners are part tim e tube well
operators and they have been granted the benefit of two
ACPs as of today. For the purpose of grant of further
prom otion, their service should be regularized. I t is not
the case that in the present case, the writ petition has
been allowed for grant of benefit of prom otion after
availing the benefit of two ACPs. The respondent-writ
petitioners have already been regularized in the year
2013-14 and for further prom otion as per G.O. dated 2nd
Decem ber, 2000, they have to be a part of regular cadre.
Hence, even this G.O. cannot be applied to the facts of
the present case and deny the benefit of grant of first and
2nd ACP to the respondent-writ petitioners, who have
been granted this benefit as per the judgment of the
Allahabad High Court dated 18.05.1994 in the case of
Su r esh Ch an d r a Tew ar i v . St at e of U.P., 1 9 9 4 SCC
On Lin e All 1 0 8 6 which has been upheld by the Hon'ble
Suprem e Court. Even this G.O., which has been relied
by the counsel for the State, has been issued by the Uttar

2024:UHC:6210-DB
19
Pradesh Governm ent with respect to the approval of the
recom mendation of the Payscale Comm ittee (1997-98).
Hence, for all intents and purposes, the present Appeals
deserve to be dismissed. Even the question of
regularization is not required to be examined as the G.O.
dated 2nd Decem ber, 2000 for further promotion after
availing the benefit of ACP-1 and ACP-2 requires an
officer/ employee to be regularly appointed. The
respondent-writ petitioners in the present case have been
regularized in the year 2013-14 and their case for future
prom otion can be considered keeping in view their
regular service with effect from the date of their
regularization.
17. Along with the affidavit dated 29.12.2016 filed
by the respondents, they have placed on record the
instructions dated 12.03.2001 issued by the Secretary,
Uttaranchal Government as Annexure No. 1, whereby the
Secretary, Uttaranchal Government has given directions
to all Principal Secretaries/ Secretaries, Uttaranchal, and
all the Heads of Departments and Officers, Uttaranchal,
with regard to approval of tim e-scale pay for state
em ployees as per the decision taken on the
recom mendations of Pay Committee (1997-99) of North-

2024:UHC:6210-DB
20
Eastern Uttar Pradesh. I n paragraph no. 3 of the said
instructions it is stated as under :
"3. Uttaranchal state was formed on 09 November
2000. Therefore, the amount from 01 January 1998 to
08 November 2000 should be paid under the main
account head-8783-I nter-State Adjustment UP
Reorganization and should be reimbursed against the
allocated budget under the relevant account head of
the department from 09 November 2000. The payment
till 08 November 2000 should be apportioned on the
basis of population by the Accountant General, Uttar
Pradesh and Uttaranchal and compensation should be
made to Uttaranchal state."
18. I n these instructions, they have followed the
Government Order dated 02.12.2000, which was issued
by the State Governm ent in continuation of the
recom mendations of the Pay Com mittee of North Eastern
Uttar Pradesh (1997-99). Hence, even after creation of
the State of Uttaranchal, the Government has accepted
the recomm endations of the Pay Committee for the year
1997-99, which have been placed on record by the
petitioner as Annexure No. A-10. Hence, once the
Government has accepted the Governm ent Order dated
02.12.2000, they cannot take a stand that paym ent of
ACP-1 and ACP-2 has been given wrongly, and they can
withdraw the said benefit after a gap of 16 years.
19. This Court has already dismissed Special Appeal
No. 223 of 2022, which had been filed by the State of
Uttarakhand, where the writ petitioners, who were

2024:UHC:6210-DB
21
declared as Primary Teachers w.e.f. 31st January, 2006,
have been granted the benefit of selection grade as per
the G.O. of 2002 and for the grant of the benefit of
selection grade, there was no condition that they should
be regularized, and the Appeal of the State has already
been dismissed and the same principle will apply in the
present case, as according to the G.O. dated 2nd
Decem ber, 2000 issued by the Uttar Pradesh
Government, the selection grade to be given after six
years or 14 years does not require appointm ent on a
regular post.
20. These Special Appeals have no m erit and are,
therefore, dismissed.
21. Pending application(s), if any, also stand
disposed of accordingly.
